answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-and-work trellis: every identity posts a refundable bond and must complete attested useful work before it can trade or vote. Like a willow trained along a trellis, reputation grows only along verified work, one branch at a time, so a fresh fake starts at the bottom with tiny limits. Fraud triggers slashing, so an attacker must pay a bond and grind out real work for each of ten thousand clones, while an honest agent pays once and earns it back. Cost, not paperwork, is the gate, and shale-solid history is what buys trust.
